distinguishing_features: Actively modulates ICCP output rather than merely inferring and alarming on corrosion-related impedance changes.
Uses localized electrolyte conductivity or cell conductance as a feed-forward indicator of splash-zone wetting.
Gates or reduces cathodic current when the conductive electrolyte bridge is absent.
Applies a wetness-dependent protection policy during transient high-oxygen-flux wetting events.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Provide sufficient cathodic protection during brief seawater-wetting events with high oxygen-reduction demand without imposing unnecessary polarization during dry periods.
parsed.viable_reason: Wetness-gated, feedback-controlled ICCP is physically implementable using local conductivity sensing, potential measurement, and adjustable rectifier output, although the candidate's dry-phase current, conductivity-proportionality, threshold, and numerical-factor claims are not generally correct.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Converting an electrical impedance or conductivity signature from passive corrosion monitoring into an active, wetting-responsive cathodic-current control policy would not have been an obvious modification of the closest prior-art monitoring approach.
